产品召回：批次、退款与联系人未作答短答题 · 5 段 · 223 词 · 5 题

官方样题 · Cambridge General Training Reading official sample · Product return · PDF 第 1 页

Answer the questions below. Choose NO MORE THAN THREE WORDS AND/OR A NUMBER from the text for each answer. Write your answers in boxes 4–8.

1Fancy Foods wishes to inform the public that pieces of metal have been found in some jars of Fancy Foods Chicken Curry (Spicy). The batches of the jars involved have numbers from J6617 to J6624. The batch number is printed on the bottom of each jar.

2If you have any jars with these batch numbers, please return them (preferably unopened) to the supermarket where you purchased them. You can also return them to the factory (Fancy Foods Retailers, Blacktown). Fancy Foods will pay $10 for each jar returned unopened and $5 for each jar already opened.

3No payment will be made for empty jars, which do not need to be returned. However, the Retailing Manager will be interested to hear from people who have consumed chicken curry from any of the above batch numbers. In particular, it will be helpful if they can give information about the place of purchase of the product.

4Jars of Fancy Foods Chicken Curry (Coconut) and Fancy Foods Chicken Curry (Mango) have not been affected and do not need to be returned.

5Fancy Foods will pay a reward of $10,000 to $50,000 for information which leads to the conviction of any person found guilty of placing metal pieces in its products. If you have such information, please contact the Customer Relations Manager, Fancy Foods Retailers, Blacktown.

4. What has been found in some Fancy Foods products?

5. Where can you find the batch number on the jars?

6. How much will you receive for an opened jar of contaminated Chicken Curry?

7. If you have eaten Chicken Curry from a jar with one of the batch numbers listed, whom should you contact?

8. What is the maximum reward Fancy Foods is offering for information about who contaminated their product?

对照答案，回到证据

第 4 题 · pieces of metal

问发现的异物，不问产品名称。三词恰好符合上限。

pieces of metal have been found in some jars

第 5 题 · the bottom；on the bottom

是罐底，不是退货地点supermarket。

The batch number is printed on the bottom of each jar.

第 6 题 · $5

opened与unopened对应两种金额，empty则不给钱。

$10 for each jar returned unopened and $5 for each jar already opened.

第 7 题 · Retailing Manager；the Retailing Manager

吃过产品找Retailing Manager；提供谁投放金属的线索找Customer Relations Manager，勿交换两个身份。

the Retailing Manager will be interested to hear from people who have consumed chicken curry

第 8 题 · $50,000

maximum取区间上限，不能取首次看到的10,000。

a reward of $10,000 to $50,000

核对原答案页

材料精读 · 内容与词句

这是一份按适用范围、退回处理、特殊情形和线索联络组织的产品召回告示。准确理解对象和条件，比把所有罐装咖喱视为同一种情况更重要。金额、产品名和联络人均属于本材料中的告示，不作为现实召回指引。

1

Fancy Foods wishes to inform the public that pieces of metal have been found in some jars of Fancy Foods Chicken Curry (Spicy). The batches of the jars involved have numbers from J6617 to J6624. The batch number is printed on the bottom of each jar.

第1段交代发现问题的产品是Spicy口味的部分罐装咖喱，涉及批号J6617至J6624，批号位于罐底。some与明确批号把范围限定住，不能扩大到该品牌所有产品。

2

If you have any jars with these batch numbers, please return them (preferably unopened) to the supermarket where you purchased them. You can also return them to the factory (Fancy Foods Retailers, Blacktown). Fancy Foods will pay $10 for each jar returned unopened and $5 for each jar already opened.

第2段说明持有这些批号产品的人可退到购买超市或工厂，preferably unopened表示最好未开封，并非已经开封就不能退。未开封每罐10美元、已开封每罐5美元是两个不同条件。

3

No payment will be made for empty jars, which do not need to be returned. However, the Retailing Manager will be interested to hear from people who have consumed chicken curry from any of the above batch numbers. In particular, it will be helpful if they can give information about the place of purchase of the product.

第3段单独处理已经吃完的情况：空罐不退款、也不必退回，但吃过有关批次产品的人仍可向零售经理提供信息，尤其是购买地点。没有退款不等于其反馈没有价值。

4

Jars of Fancy Foods Chicken Curry (Coconut) and Fancy Foods Chicken Curry (Mango) have not been affected and do not need to be returned.

第4段明确Coconut和Mango两种口味未受影响，无须退回；这与第一段指定Spicy口味共同界定召回边界。

5

Fancy Foods will pay a reward of $10,000 to $50,000 for information which leads to the conviction of any person found guilty of placing metal pieces in its products. If you have such information, please contact the Customer Relations Manager, Fancy Foods Retailers, Blacktown.

第5段转为征集导致涉案人员被定罪的线索，奖金范围与普通退货退款不同。此处联络的是客户关系经理，不能与前面接收已食用产品信息的零售经理混同。

词语与搭配

wishes to inform the public

谨此告知公众

正式告示中礼貌地引出通知内容；wish to并非表示消息还没有发生。

preferably unopened

最好尚未开封

preferably表达优先选择，不是必须满足的绝对条件。

the place of purchase

购买地点

purchase在这里是购买这一行为，place of说明行为发生地点。

leads to the conviction

促成定罪

lead to后接名词；conviction此处是司法定罪，不是个人的坚定信念。

句子精读

If you have any jars with these batch numbers, please return them (preferably unopened) to the supermarket where you purchased them.

如果你持有任何标有这些批号的罐装产品，请把它们退回购买它们的超市，最好保持未开封状态。

If从句限定指令适用的人；these batch numbers回指前段范围。them指相关罐装产品；where引出修饰the supermarket的地点关系。括号中的preferably是偏好条件。

No payment will be made for empty jars, which do not need to be returned.

空罐不予退款，而且也无须退回。

主句的被动语态把重点放在退款安排；which补充说明empty jars，do not need to表示没有退回的必要，不是禁止退回。两项安排只适用于空罐。

读完讲解，可以把原文连起来再读一次；想保留的词句可使用已有收藏功能。

Rethinking the Past · 发现怎样改变既有认识未作答选择题 / 句尾匹配 · 3 段 · 285 词 · 3 题 · 同篇原文另有裁切

真题 · Cambridge IELTS 21 Academic · PDF 第 69 页

按原题号作答。保留考试原文与题目难度；以下是连续原段裁切，未改写原文。

原第1–3段连续裁切；第27题的second paragraph仍指原文第2段。句尾匹配保留A–F完整选项，不删干扰项。

原文片段 · 1It is by now a truism that the story of human evolution is being rethought. Discoveries have come thick and fast over the last decade or so, and these have forced us to rethink many crucial points, such as how old our species is - about 300,000 years old as opposed to 200,000 - and what extinct hominins, such as our cousins the Neanderthals, were really like. But because there are so many species and eras involved, it's hard to discern the common threads linking them.

原文片段 · 2However, I do think it's possible to draw out some overall messages from the blizzard of archaeological finds in recent years. Two things stand out to me. One is the growing evidence that many supposedly 'advanced' behaviours, such as architecture and art, can be traced much further back in time than we thought, often to hominin species that existed before modern humans. And the other is that we have badly misunderstood gender roles in prehistoric societies, imposing patriarchal values onto cultures that had very different ideas about how women should behave.

原文片段 · 3Let's start with architecture. At Kalambo Falls in Zambia, researchers found buried logs that had been shaped with stone tools so that they interlocked. They seem to have once been part of a larger structure, perhaps a building. This would be unsurprising if they weren't 476,000 years old. That's almost 200,000 years before our species, Homo sapiens, evolved. Extinct hominins also managed to settle in extreme places. For instance, we now know that extinct hominins such as the Denisovans lived on the frozen heights of high-altitude regions 200,000 years ago - upending the old notion that such environments were only settled by modern humans around 3,600 years ago.

共用选项 · 原题 31、32

  • A. Homo sapiens emerged at an earlier point in time than experts previously believed.
  • B. previous assumptions about who had power in the prehistoric world were inaccurate.
  • C. gender roles in extinct hominin species were different from those in Homo sapiens societies.
  • D. experts may have been mistaken about who looked for food in early human communities.
  • E. Homo sapiens was probably not the only species capable of sophisticated workmanship.
  • F. other species managed to survive in harsh environments before the arrival of Homo sapiens.

27. What is the writer doing in the second paragraph?

Choose the correct letter, A, B, C or D.

  • A. pinpointing some key changes in our understanding of prehistory
  • B. outlining some aspects of prehistory which are still poorly understood
  • C. summarising some attitudes towards recent archaeological revelations
  • D. giving an overview of some current disagreements among archaeologists

31. The findings at Kalambo Falls revealed that

Complete each sentence with the correct ending, A–F, below.

32. Evidence from high-altitude regions suggests that

Complete each sentence with the correct ending, A–F, below.

对照答案，回到证据

第 27 题 · A

作者归纳两项认识变化，不是在罗列考古学家的争议；second paragraph指原第2段。

Two things stand out to me. One is ... advanced behaviours ... much further back ... And the other ... misunderstood gender roles

第 31 题 · E

石器加工并互锁的木材早于现代人，支撑其他物种也能进行复杂制作；不是说现代人提前出现。

buried logs ... shaped with stone tools so that they interlocked ... 476,000 years old ... before our species

第 32 题 · F

extinct hominins先在严寒高地生活，对应other species在Homo sapiens之前适应恶劣环境。

the Denisovans lived on the frozen heights ... 200,000 years ago

核对原答案页

材料精读 · 内容与词句

作者把大量考古发现归纳成两条需要重看的认识：某些被视为先进的行为比过去想象的更早出现，对史前性别分工的看法也可能受当代预设影响。这里主要展开建筑和极端环境定居的例子，注意区分发现本身与研究者对用途的推测。

原文片段 · 1

It is by now a truism that the story of human evolution is being rethought. Discoveries have come thick and fast over the last decade or so, and these have forced us to rethink many crucial points, such as how old our species is - about 300,000 years old as opposed to 200,000 - and what extinct hominins, such as our cousins the Neanderthals, were really like. But because there are so many species and eras involved, it's hard to discern the common threads linking them.

接连出现的发现改变了对人类起源年代及已灭绝人族成员的理解，但物种和年代众多，整体联系并不容易辨认。truism 表示已经被反复承认的说法；common threads 是贯穿材料的共同线索，作者接下来要从碎片发现中提炼这些联系。

原文片段 · 2

However, I do think it's possible to draw out some overall messages from the blizzard of archaeological finds in recent years. Two things stand out to me. One is the growing evidence that many supposedly 'advanced' behaviours, such as architecture and art, can be traced much further back in time than we thought, often to hominin species that existed before modern humans. And the other is that we have badly misunderstood gender roles in prehistoric societies, imposing patriarchal values onto cultures that had very different ideas about how women should behave.

作者明确以 I do think 和 to me 提出自己的归纳：建筑、艺术等行为的历史可能追溯到现代人之前；史前女性角色则被后来的父权观念误读。supposedly 给 advanced 加上距离感，提醒读者所谓先进本身也带有分类与评价。

原文片段 · 3

Let's start with architecture. At Kalambo Falls in Zambia, researchers found buried logs that had been shaped with stone tools so that they interlocked. They seem to have once been part of a larger structure, perhaps a building. This would be unsurprising if they weren't 476,000 years old. That's almost 200,000 years before our species, Homo sapiens, evolved. Extinct hominins also managed to settle in extreme places. For instance, we now know that extinct hominins such as the Denisovans lived on the frozen heights of high-altitude regions 200,000 years ago - upending the old notion that such environments were only settled by modern humans around 3,600 years ago.

赞比亚木构件的加工与咬合显示它们可能属于更大的结构，但 perhaps a building 仍是对用途的推测。476,000年前的年代使发现尤其突出，因为比现代人出现还早。高海拔地区的古人族居住证据则挑战了这类环境很晚才被占据的旧想法。

词语与搭配

come thick and fast

大量而接连不断地出现

形容发现出现得多且频繁；是较生动的固定表达，不是说发现物本身很厚。

the common threads

共同线索

threads 比喻连接不同发现的主题；作者想理解它们共同改变了什么认识。

can be traced much further back in time

可以追溯到久远得多的过去

be traced back 表示追溯起源；much 修饰比较级 further，强调与旧估计的差距。

imposing patriarchal values onto cultures

把父权价值观强加到其他文化的解释上

这里指用后来研究者的观念解读古代文化，并非说这些研究者真的改变了史前社会。

句子精读

One is the growing evidence that many supposedly 'advanced' behaviours, such as architecture and art, can be traced much further back in time than we thought, often to hominin species that existed before modern humans.

其中一点是，越来越多证据显示，建筑和艺术等许多所谓先进的行为，可以追溯到比我们原先想象久远得多的年代，往往追溯到现代人出现之前就已存在的人族物种。

One 指作者归纳出的两条认识之一。第一个 that 引出 evidence 的具体内容，such as 插入例子；than we thought 给出比较基准。最后的 that existed 修饰 hominin species，限定这些物种所处的时代。

At Kalambo Falls in Zambia, researchers found buried logs that had been shaped with stone tools so that they interlocked.

在赞比亚的卡兰博瀑布，研究人员发现了埋藏的木料，这些木料曾用石器加工，从而能够相互咬合。

that had been shaped 修饰 logs，过去完成时表示加工早于研究人员发现。so that 引出加工所达到的目的或效果，they 回指木料。句子先报告材料及加工特征，后文才推测它们可能的用途。

读完讲解，可以把原文连起来再读一次；想保留的词句可使用已有收藏功能。

Rethinking the Past · 艺术年代、研究争议与脑容量未作答观点判断 YNNG · 2 段 · 292 词 · 6 题 · 同篇原文另有裁切

真题 · Cambridge IELTS 21 Academic · PDF 第 69, 70 页

按原题号作答。保留考试原文与题目难度；以下是连续原段裁切，未改写原文。

保留原第4–5段；第5段跨PDF69–70页已按原句接合，不增删论证。NG已核对整篇文章。

原文片段 · 1Art also seems to have been invented by older hominins. We have had evidence for a long time now that Neanderthals painted on cave walls. Even earlier species, such as Homo erectus, may also have made art, for example by engraving patterns on shells. By far the most contentious claim in this area is that Homo naledi made art. H. naledi lived around 250,000 years ago, making it a contemporary of our species. However, it had quite a small brain, typical of older hominins - and was therefore, according to palaeoanthropological dogma, incapable of complex behaviours. Nevertheless, in the Rising Star cave system in South Africa where the H. naledi remains were found, researchers have found what seem to be etchings - resembling rudimentary artwork- on the cave walls, though these have yet to be firmly dated.

原文片段 · 2To say these claims about H. naledi are controversial is to understate the situation. Many experts say the evidence presented so far is completely inadequate to support them. The dispute has only been heightened by the way the results were released, in a non-traditional journal that publishes peer reviews publicly alongside the paper. My views on the H. naledi controversy are complicated. I do think more evidence is needed: in particular with regard to the dating of the etchings. At the same time, I think the species' small brains are a distraction. Palaeoanthropologists got fixated on brain size because it was what they could see: if what you have is skeletons, then all you know about brains are their shapes and sizes. But other properties, such as the brain's internal wiring, are surely equally important and may explain how a species like H. naledi might have been capable of complex behaviours, despite their small brains.

35. It seems likely that the Neanderthals' cave paintings were the first examples of artwork ever created.

Do the following statements agree with the views/claims of the writer? Write YES, NO or NOT GIVEN.

36. It is very rare to find prehistoric artwork carved onto shells.

Do the following statements agree with the views/claims of the writer? Write YES, NO or NOT GIVEN.

37. The methods which the researchers used to examine the Rising Star cave system were rather unconventional.

Do the following statements agree with the views/claims of the writer? Write YES, NO or NOT GIVEN.

38. It is unclear how old the etchings in the Rising Star cave system are.

Do the following statements agree with the views/claims of the writer? Write YES, NO or NOT GIVEN.

39. The means used to publicise the findings from the Rising Star cave system added to the controversy that surrounds them.

Do the following statements agree with the views/claims of the writer? Write YES, NO or NOT GIVEN.

40. The size of H. naledi brains is a key factor in the question of whether these hominins were able to produce art.

Do the following statements agree with the views/claims of the writer? Write YES, NO or NOT GIVEN.

对照答案，回到证据

第 35 题 · NO

Even earlier直接给出更早物种可能作画的证据，反驳尼安德特人必为最早的倾向判断。

Even earlier species, such as Homo erectus, may also have made art

第 36 题 · NOT GIVEN

原文只举贝壳刻纹这一例子，全文没有very rare的频率判断。

may also have made art, for example by engraving patterns on shells

第 37 题 · NOT GIVEN

non-traditional修饰发表结果的期刊，不是考察洞穴的方法；全文未评价实地研究方法是否反常。

the way the results were released, in a non-traditional journal

第 38 题 · YES

have yet to be firmly dated表示尚未可靠定年，正好支持unclear how old。

these have yet to be firmly dated ... more evidence is needed ... dating of the etchings

第 39 题 · YES

publicise findings对应results released；added to controversy对应dispute heightened。

The dispute has only been heightened by the way the results were released

第 40 题 · NO

该题问作者观点，不是前人dogma。作者明确把小脑容量称为干扰焦点，不能把先引述的旧教条当作者结论。

I think the species' small brains are a distraction ... internal wiring ... equally important

核对原答案页

材料精读 · 内容与词句

作者讨论早期人族艺术的证据及 Homo naledi 争议，既要求刻痕年代得到更可靠确认，也反对只凭脑容量判断复杂行为能力。核心张力是证据需要加强，但评估证据的既有框架本身也值得反思。

原文片段 · 1

Art also seems to have been invented by older hominins. We have had evidence for a long time now that Neanderthals painted on cave walls. Even earlier species, such as Homo erectus, may also have made art, for example by engraving patterns on shells. By far the most contentious claim in this area is that Homo naledi made art. H. naledi lived around 250,000 years ago, making it a contemporary of our species. However, it had quite a small brain, typical of older hominins - and was therefore, according to palaeoanthropological dogma, incapable of complex behaviours. Nevertheless, in the Rising Star cave system in South Africa where the H. naledi remains were found, researchers have found what seem to be etchings - resembling rudimentary artwork- on the cave walls, though these have yet to be firmly dated.

对不同物种的证据强度并不相同：尼安德特人壁画已有证据，更早物种制作艺术则以 may 表示可能。关于 Homo naledi 的说法争议最大，因为传统观点把小脑容量与无法进行复杂行为联系起来；洞壁刻痕看似艺术，但仍没有确定年代。contemporary 指与现代人这一物种在时间上并存。

原文片段 · 2

To say these claims about H. naledi are controversial is to understate the situation. Many experts say the evidence presented so far is completely inadequate to support them. The dispute has only been heightened by the way the results were released, in a non-traditional journal that publishes peer reviews publicly alongside the paper. My views on the H. naledi controversy are complicated. I do think more evidence is needed: in particular with regard to the dating of the etchings. At the same time, I think the species' small brains are a distraction. Palaeoanthropologists got fixated on brain size because it was what they could see: if what you have is skeletons, then all you know about brains are their shapes and sizes. But other properties, such as the brain's internal wiring, are surely equally important and may explain how a species like H. naledi might have been capable of complex behaviours, despite their small brains.

争论既涉及证据是否足够，也受到公开同行评议这一发表方式的影响。作者承认需要更强的年代证据，却认为脑容量争论容易分散注意力：骨骼让研究者容易看到形状和大小，内部连接等重要特征反而难以直接得知。最后提出可能解释，没有宣告已经证实 Homo naledi 会创作艺术。

词语与搭配

have yet to be firmly dated

尚未得到可靠断代

have yet to 表示某事截至叙述时尚未完成；dated 在考古语境中指确定年代。

the evidence presented so far

迄今提出的证据

so far 将判断限定在目前可获得的材料，保留以后出现新证据的可能。

with regard to

关于，就……而言

原文把需要更多证据的范围收窄到刻痕年代，而不是笼统否定全部发现。

got fixated on brain size

过于执着于脑容量

fixated on 带有注意力被单一因素占据的意味，是作者对研究倾向的批评。

句子精读

Palaeoanthropologists got fixated on brain size because it was what they could see: if what you have is skeletons, then all you know about brains are their shapes and sizes.

古人类学家过于执着于脑容量，因为这是他们能观察到的东西：如果手头只有骨骼，那么对大脑所能知道的也就只有形状和大小。

because 解释注意力集中于脑容量的原因。冒号后用 if 条件句展开限制；what you have 作主语，all you know about brains 表示所知的全部内容。这里说的是材料可见性如何影响研究视角。

But other properties, such as the brain's internal wiring, are surely equally important and may explain how a species like H. naledi might have been capable of complex behaviours, despite their small brains.

但其他特征，例如大脑内部的连接方式，想必也同样重要，并且可能解释像 Homo naledi 这样的物种为何虽脑容量较小，却仍可能具备复杂行为能力。

such as 插入具体特征，how 从句作 explain 的宾语。may explain 与 might have been 都保留可能性；despite 引出小脑容量这一看似相反的条件。surely 显示作者的判断语气，不把后面的推测变成定论。

2The 'birds are dinosaurs' theory was first developed by English palaeontologist Thomas Huxley (1825–1895). According to some accounts, one evening Huxley went to dinner still thinking about a mystery dinosaur bone in his lab. He knew he was dealing with the lower leg bone (tibia) of a meat-eating, two-legged dinosaur belonging to the classification known as theropods, but attached to the tibia was an unidentified extra bone. On the menu that evening was quail, a small bird similar to a pheasant, and Huxley noticed the same strange bone, attached to the quail tibia on his plate. He later realised that it was in fact the bird's anklebone. More importantly, Huxley concluded that its forms in both dinosaur and bird skeletons were so similar that they must be closely related.

3Huxley's idea fell out of favour for fifty years following the 1916 publication of The Origin of Birds by the Danish doctor Gerhard Heilmann. During this time, Heilmann’s theory was widely accepted. Heilmann had noted that two-legged, meat-eating dinosaurs lacked collarbones. In later evolutionary stages these bones fuse together to form the distinctive 'Y'-shaped bone in a bird's neck, known as the furcula. Heilmann proposed the notion that such a feature could not be lost and then re-evolve at a later date, so dinosaurs could not be the ancestors of birds.

4Then, in the late 1960s, John Ostrom from Yale University in the USA, noted 22 features in the skeletons of meat-eating dinosaurs that were also found in birds and nowhere else. This reset the thinking on bird ancestry and once again Huxley’s ideas caught the attention of the scientific community. Subsequent work has found up to 85 characteristics that tie dinosaurs and birds together. But what of Heilmann's missing bones? It turns out that not only did many dinosaurs have collarbones, these were also fused together into a furcula. Unfortunately for Heilmann, the fossil evidence was somewhat lacking in his day, and the few furculae that had been found were misidentified, usually as belly ribs.

5US ornithologist Alan Feduccia and palaeontologist Larry Martin are two vocal opponents of the dinosaur theory. They contend that birds evolved from some unknown reptile at a time long before dinosaurs. Their reasoning is that flight is most likely to have started from a tree-climbing ancestor, yet all the proposed dinosaurian ancestors were ground-dwellers. But the dino-bird supporters contend that an unknown dinosaurian bird-ancestor could have been tree-dwelling, or that birds evolved flight from the ground up by chasing and leaping after insects. Most of Feduccia and Martin's case against the 'birds-are-dinosaurs' hypothesis is based on differences between birds and dinosaurs. Supporters of cladistics, however, maintain that differences between organisms do not matter, as it is the similarities between them that count. Evolution dictates that organisms will change through time, so it is only the features which persist that carry useful information about their origins.

6Most people on either side of the debate do accept, however, that the ancient winged creature known as Archaeopteryx is an ancestor of today’s birds. This is in spite of the fact that its form is distinctly non-bird-like, with a long bony tail, and teeth instead of a beak. The 'birds-are-dinosaurs' supporters contend that, if clearly-preserved feathers had not been found alongside two of the seven Archaeopteryx specimens, it would probably have been identified as a small dinosaur. However, Archaeopteryx does have some bird-like features, such as a furcula and bird-like feet, that suggest that it is too bird-like to be considered a dinosaur.

7Over the last few decades several dinosaurs with bird-like features and primitive birds with dinosaur-like features have been found in several countries, connecting Archaeopteryx back to dinosaurs, and forwards to modern birds. Sinosauropteryx, excavated from 130-million-year-old rocks in northeast China, is one example. It has a dinosaur skeleton surrounded by a halo of fuzz, thought to be primitive feathers. And a reassessment of other dinosaurs reveals such bird-like features as hollow bones and a foot with three functional toes, characteristics that appeared over 50 million years before Archaeopteryx took to the air. And Rahonavis, a primitive bird from Madagascar is more bird-like than Archaeopteryx, yet retains some distinctive dinosaur features, including a long and vicious claw at the end of its wing. Over a century since Huxley's discovery, it seems that cladistics may have finally settled the 'dino-bird' debate.

第7段沿两个方向补充过渡联系：一端是带鸟样特征的恐龙，另一端是仍保留恐龙特征的早期鸟类。中华龙鸟周围的绒状物在文中被认为可能是原始羽毛；Rahonavis则展示更接近鸟类却仍有独特爪子的组合。结尾的谨慎语气与前面持续积累的证据相呼应。

句子精读

The 'birds-are-dinosaurs' supporters contend that, if clearly-preserved feathers had not been found alongside two of the seven Archaeopteryx specimens, it would probably have been identified as a small dinosaur.

支持“鸟类源自恐龙”观点的人认为，如果七个始祖鸟标本中的两个旁边没有发现保存清晰的羽毛，它很可能就会被认作一种小型恐龙。

contend that引出这一派的判断；if...had not been found与would probably have been identified构成对过去情况的反事实设想。it指始祖鸟；probably保留可能性，句子不是说这些标本实际上都曾被误认。

Over the last few decades several dinosaurs with bird-like features and primitive birds with dinosaur-like features have been found in several countries, connecting Archaeopteryx back to dinosaurs, and forwards to modern birds.

在此前几十年间，人们在几个国家发现了多种具有鸟样特征的恐龙，以及保留恐龙样特征的原始鸟类；这些发现把始祖鸟与更早的恐龙及更晚的现代鸟类联系起来。

两个并列名词组dinosaurs with...与primitive birds with...共同作主语；have been found强调发现。connecting...补充这些发现形成的联系，back和forwards描述演化联系的两个方向，不是说始祖鸟个体向两个方向变化。
